scenes.title: AI 시대에 쌓아 온 실력의 가치
lines: Hello. This is Yamyam Coding.

AI has begun writing code and creating game scenes. What value will our years of programming, drawing and game-design experience have? We will trace how development tools have changed, consider automation and work, then use an actual shop system to see where a developer’s judgment matters.
This discussion builds on a video by Wild Ox Studios about AI and the games industry. His starting point is the work we have learned to delegate to development tools.

scenes.title: 사람이 쓰기 편한 개발 도구
lines: Epic Games’ Unreal Engine is a useful example of that change.
Unreal has long developed visual tools that people can work with comfortably. Kismet and Blueprints are examples.
In Blueprints, you arrange nodes representing functions and connect them to define behavior: when a door opens, how a character attacks, or what happens in response to an event.
A major advantage is that designers unfamiliar with writing text code can build game behavior themselves.
The original creator sees this as Unreal evolving around human-friendly workflows.
He views Nanite and Lumen in a similar context. As the engine handles more of the complexity behind a scene, creators can concentrate on composing it and judging the result.

Enabling a feature does not automatically solve performance and quality problems in every project. Still, tools have increasingly taken over complex, repetitive work while people compose scenes and evaluate them.

scenes.title: 사람과 AI가 도구에 접근하는 방식
lines: Until now, people directly operated those tools. Delegating tasks to AI introduces another requirement.
An interface that people find easy to see and manipulate may differ from one that lets AI read and modify a project effectively.

People can understand a structure from the placement of nodes and the flow of connections. To delegate work to AI, we must clearly expose available functions, permitted changes and ways to check the result.
Alongside a human-friendly editor, we need ways for AI to call functions and inspect their outcomes. This is entering the design of next-generation engines.

scenes.title: UE6 전환 계획과 MCP
lines: Epic’s announced UE6 plans include Verse, a new gameplay architecture and connections between AI tools and engine functionality through MCP. Blueprints and Actors are planned to remain in early UE6, then be replaced gradually with migration tools as the new architecture matures. This does not mean Blueprints disappear immediately.
Here, think of MCP as a protocol connecting AI to information and functions provided by external tools.
Instead of merely answering development questions, an AI workflow can inspect a project, execute an available function and check what happened.
The change therefore goes beyond putting a chat window beside the developer. It involves adapting the engine and development process for working with AI.

scenes.title: 코드 작성에서 완성 책임으로
lines: Separate from that long-term engine plan, reports are also describing changes within production teams. Bloomberg recently reported that Epic’s Disney collaboration was delayed and developers were asked to expand their use of AI.
The original video interprets such news as a sign that manually writing every line may no longer be development’s default assumption.
The pace and extent of change will vary by company. But it is worth considering how expectations of developers may change.
Alongside the ability to implement a feature directly, the ability to use tools, including AI, to build accurately, verify and finish a product may become increasingly important.

scenes.title: 도구가 달라져도 남는 판단
lines: Game developers have already experienced changes in the skills needed when tools take over work once performed directly.
The original video cites the evolution of tools such as Substance Painter, Photoshop and ZBrush.
A texture is an image applied to a model’s surface. UV coordinates determine which part of the image belongs on which face. Think of an unfolded paper box.

Earlier workflows required painting color and detail while looking at flattened UV layouts. Newer tools made it common to paint directly on a model, work with several material properties together and automate repetitive work.
Transferring details from a high-resolution model to another model also became part of production.
When tools change, the route to the same result changes, along with the expertise expected in a workplace.
Traditional methods can still be sufficient in some situations. But participating in a new production process requires learning its tools and workflows.
This does not make the time spent learning older skills meaningless.
Understanding form, distinguishing materials and judging quality still matter. What changes is how that understanding becomes a result.
The original creator places AI in this longer history. Yet one further issue matters: judgment remaining useful does not mean everyone’s job stays intact.

scenes.title: 자동화의 이익과 일자리 변화
lines: Manufacturing, which experienced automation before game development, makes that distinction clearer.
The original creator says he worked in a factory for eleven years and participated in making processes more efficient.
When machines take over repetitive tasks, some people escape difficult, monotonous work. The change can be positive if they can move into another role.
But not everyone finds another job.
Sometimes the change goes beyond making a task easier and reduces the number of people employed to do it. Productivity gains and individual employment insecurity can coexist.
To understand automation’s impact, we must consider both what becomes easier and whose work shrinks or requires a different role.

scenes.title: 손으로 만든 물건의 가치
lines: Does a shrinking share of jobs necessarily mean the skills learned through that work lose all their value?
The original video uses handmade clothing and furniture as examples.
Even after mass production became widespread, some people continued seeking handmade furniture and carefully carved ornament.
Such objects are not judged only by their function. Materials, workmanship, attention to finish and the identity of their maker can contribute to their value.
Of course, handmade does not automatically mean better. Distinctive quality and expression must accompany the fact that a person made it.
Making an object with the same function differs from giving it distinctive value. This is the distinction the original creator emphasizes.

scenes.title: 존재하는 결과와 특별한 경험
lines: We can consider the same distinction in digital work. As producing an output gets cheaper, its mere existence may be less exceptional.
People may instead look more closely at the choices and intentions behind it.
Similar kinds of pictures can feel different depending on their composition, intended atmosphere and expression.
Games are no different.
There is a gap between a game running and a player having a distinctive experience.

Even when the same character receives the same potion, changing a number feels different from combining a character reaction, sound and reward display. Choosing what to show and when changes the experience.

scenes.title: Unity Spark가 여는 제작 기회
lines: Some people wanted to test those choices but were held back by programming. That is one opportunity AI creation tools could expand.
Unity Spark illustrates this direction.

Unity describes Spark as a service for creating and sharing games in a browser without prior Unity or game-development experience. As checked on October14,2026, its official page says it is coming soon and offers a waitlist.
Unity also provides AI tools in its existing development environment for answering questions, writing code and performing editor tasks.
The original creator connects this direction with more people becoming creators, as on platforms such as Roblox.
Some experienced players can explain precisely what their favorite genre is missing.
Some artists have a world they want to create but have been unable to start because of programming.
AI-assisted tools could give these people more opportunities to try their ideas in a working form.
However, being able to start a game and finishing a polished game are different things.
A wider entrance can be welcome. Yet the process that someone can now begin easily may also be work another person has spent years learning and loving.

scenes.title: 창작 과정이 사라질 때 느끼는 감정
lines: For those people, changes in the creative process can bring a sense of loss alongside opportunity.
That feeling is why the original video introduces indie developer Thomas Brush.
Thomas Brush is a developer behind games including Pinstripe, Neversong and Twisted Tower.
The supplied subtitles describe him feeling sad that coding, animating and digital drawing—things he has done since childhood—seem to be pushed aside in the industry.
That feeling is understandable.
We do not always learn an activity solely because we like its output.
We may learn programming because we love writing code, fixing mistakes and finally seeing an idea behave as intended.
We may love drawing because of the process of building an image through lines and layers of color.
The process itself was a source of joy and part of an identity.

scenes.title: 직접 만들고 확인하는 경험
lines: The Wild Ox Studios creator also explains how making things was connected to his identity.
He says he encountered Newgrounds and Flash, learned ActionScript and began programming in BASIC on a Commodore64. His interests later expanded to Unreal and Quake mods, Source and UDK.
He describes working with music, audio, advertising and filmmaking before moving into automation and robotics.
Across these fields, he valued using principles he understood to make something, then seeing it move or hearing it produce sound.
After accumulating those experiences, it is natural to have complicated feelings when the process changes dramatically.

scenes.title: 변하는 산업과 남아 있는 기술
lines: He therefore sympathizes with that sadness, but distinguishes changes in familiar methods from the disappearance of human skill.
People still forge objects from metal and make furniture by hand.
A craft’s share of industrial work and its working methods can change without eliminating the skill or everything it can express.
He looks at painting similarly.
Painting continues despite photography and digital tools. People still admire particular artists’ expression and seek their work.
Bringing this perspective to digital work raises the question of where its value lies.
The creator asks how digital works can retain lasting value. There have been attempts such as NFTs, but being digital does not by itself determine a work’s value.

scenes.title: 작은 팀이 완성하는 상호작용
lines: Games offer a special case for that question because we can directly experience what a digital creation gives a player.
Alongside art, music and story, games contain structures that respond to the player’s actions.
We do not simply watch. We move, choose, fail and try again.
Many different skills are connected into one experience.
When one person or a small team completes such an experience, we should consider what they created as well as which tools they used.
The original creator welcomes the possibility that AI could expand the expressive scope of small teams.
At the same time, he says the effects of how those tools are used also matter.

scenes.title: 자동화와 창작의 책임
lines: To consider those effects, the original video returns to the automated production environments discussed earlier.
It revisits cars and mass-produced furniture used in everyday life.
Machines are deeply involved in producing many goods. Consumers do not always examine whether a person directly performed every step.
The creator says he saw factories where a small number of people supervised equipment producing large quantities.
He sees a similar change now expanding beyond physical labor to intellectual work such as coding and design.
This comparison helps explain the broader direction of automation.
But the existence of past automation does not answer every present-day question.
The conditions under which creators’ work is used, the rights in outputs and how the burden of change falls on workers must each be considered.
We must consider both what a tool can do and appropriate ways to use it. Taking responsibility for an outcome includes these judgments.

scenes.title: 작동하는 시연에서 제품까지
lines: In development, that responsibility reveals the difference between getting a feature to work once and completing a product people can continue using.
The original video introduces a point from Thomas Brush along these lines:
AI may make it easier to produce working software in one attempt, but that does not mean everyone can make a finished product.
The important word is product.
Suppose a button appears, a character moves and an enemy attacks.

Imagine a game where players paint the ground. Getting a character to move and leave paint demonstrates an important feature. That screen alone does not establish multiplayer behavior or the quality of an entire match.
Confirming movement and painting is a meaningful first step.
But a product people keep using must handle conditions absent from that first demonstration.

scenes.title: 상점의 정상 동작과 예외
lines: Let us return to the potion shop. This time, we will examine the conditions governing a purchase rather than how its reward is presented.
Suppose we asked AI to implement buying items with gold.
Pressing the button subtracts gold and adds an item. One attempt seems to work.
The character has100 gold and a potion costs30. Buying one should leave70 gold and add one potion to the inventory. Both the charge and the item grant must be correct.
What if gold is insufficient? What if the inventory is full? Could repeated button presses process a purchase twice?
Now set the balance to20. The same button should reject the purchase. The balance must remain20 and no potion should be added.

We must also define what happens when the bag is full. Here, we reject the purchase and leave the gold unchanged. The player must not lose money without receiving an item. After checking money and capacity, we must inspect the request itself.

scenes.title: 조건과 책임을 정하는 개발자
lines: Processing the same request twice is one example. A player asking to buy twice differs from one request arriving twice because of a communication problem. The latter requires a way to recognize and process the request only once.
In multiplayer, we must consider differences between players’ states. Results should also survive saving and restarting.
A check mark on screen does not verify persistence or multiplayer. We must reconnect, compare states and examine failures.
Who defines these conditions and decides what to check?
This is where a developer’s understanding matters.
Faster code generation does not automatically clarify a system’s requirements and responsibilities.
The original creator says understanding requirements and designing complex systems matter in his work as a software engineer.
The more we delegate to AI, the more clearly we must describe the result and its evaluation criteria. We can now consider how to put those criteria into an AI workflow.

scenes.title: AI 작업 흐름에도 필요한 검증
lines: We can turn the shop’s purchase conditions into requirements and connect stages that implement and check them.
An AI can read requirements, change code, run tests and revise failures.
The process may need information from previous work, evaluation of the current result and verification through actual execution.
Yet connecting many stages does not automatically produce a good product.
If implementation follows an incorrect requirement and verification repeats that same assumption, a wrong result can pass several stages.
If duplicate requests never appear in the shop requirements, a test that only checks one successful purchase may miss the problem.
Look beyond a passing result to what was tested. Checking normal purchases, insufficient funds, inventory capacity and repeated delivery of one request can expose gaps.
People who understand development from beginning to end therefore still have an important role.
They can notice missing conditions, decide where to look and anticipate interactions between features. Even after all these checks pass, one question remains: is the game fun?

scenes.title: 재미를 판단하는 감각과 구현
lines: Experience gained through playing games can help answer that question.
The original creator suggests that experienced players may recognize what creates enjoyment and what interrupts its flow.
They may explain which rewards feel satisfying, when combat gets boring or what feels unresponsive.
That judgment can help when making games with AI.
Even two jumps covering the same distance can feel different if one responds late. Adjusting the response and playing again turns a vague feeling into a concrete condition we can change.
However, explaining fun and implementing it reliably are abilities that should develop together.
An appealing feature does not automatically solve persistence or performance. Technical stability alone does not make a game fun either.

scenes.title: 앞으로의 발전은 전망이다
lines: Advances in AI tools may also help narrow the gap between a sense of fun and a reliable implementation.
The original creator expects better AI coordination and verification to expand its role in building more complex products.
That is a forecast, not a claim that the process is solved for every product today. Even if we delegate more implementation, choosing the experience we want to create remains important.

scenes.title: 월드 오브 워크래프트의 미술 선택
lines: To consider the value of that choice, think of a game remembered for something other than how closely it resembles reality.
The original creator’s example is World of Warcraft.
He says he enjoys the game and emphasizes its enduring art direction, sound and atmosphere.
Images that look like direct copies of reality are not the only ones people can love for years.
Exaggerated shapes, painted-looking textures, colors and music suited to a world can combine into a distinctive impression.
The point is not to judge a work solely by whether it uses a particular rendering technique.
It is to consider the visual choices and how well they fit the game’s experience.

scenes.title: 사실성과 개성은 같은 기준이 아니다
lines: Therefore, the ability to create more realistic images does not mean every game must pursue the same direction.
The comparison on screen changes the presentation of the same character in the same place. Instead of declaring one universally better, we should ask which fits our intended world and experience.
Some games impress through their resemblance to reality. Others remain memorable because they depict worlds in impossible ways.
The original creator believes the latter choices can preserve a work’s individuality over time.
He also predicts that as AI makes outputs easier to produce, audiences may pay closer attention to individuality and deliberate choices.

scenes.title: 기억되는 제작자의 감각
lines: Remembering that individuality can lead us to the names and faces of the people who made those choices.
The original video cites the music and art of Halo and The Elder Scrolls as examples of creators’ sensibilities being remembered.
When we love a work, we may want more than a similar output from just anyone.
We become curious about what its creator will show us next.
We look forward to their choice of scenes, sounds and experiences.
That trust does not arise simply from producing more outputs. It grows through consistent choices and responsibility for their results.

scenes.title: 축적한 기술로 도구를 지휘하기
lines: Skills acquired through making things can inform the judgment behind that trust. That is why the original creator encourages people like Thomas Brush to consider other possibilities too.
Skills you developed directly can remain a basis for evaluating new tools.
You can explain why a form in an AI-generated image looks awkward.
You can read generated code and identify a problem that may emerge later even though it works now.
You can judge what to remove from a generated scene so its intended emotion becomes clearer.
The shop illustrates this too. Finding a missing purchase condition and improving the timing of a reward call on different experiences and judgments.
Even when directing several AI tools, your choices about what to accept and what to change will show in the outcome.

scenes.title: 강력한 공구를 다루는 숙련
lines: The original video compares this relationship to a tool and a skilled operator. More power still requires judgment about where and how much to use.
A power tool can speed up work. But without knowing the force required, the material and when to stop, you can damage a screw or a component.
A tool’s increased power does not replace its user’s understanding.
A skilled person understands what a tool can do and adjusts its power to the task.
A similar change can occur in development tools.
Delegating parts of previously manual work lets a person handle a wider scope.
That makes it important to judge what to delegate, which results to accept and where to intervene. When many people use the same tools, some problems also extend beyond individual expertise.

scenes.title: 새 도구와 함께 바뀌는 규칙
lines: Shared standards and responsibilities are one such problem. The original creator compares this with changes to roads and rules after cars appeared.
New technology changes more than its operating instructions.
Accidents occur, responsibility must be assigned and standards are needed so people can use it together.
AI-assisted development and creation will involve adjustments to working practices, responsibility, rights and expectations alongside technical performance.
We are in the middle of that change.
We do not yet know precisely which tasks will be automated or which roles will shrink or grow. But even amid uncertainty, we can use the knowledge we already have.

scenes.title: 배운 실력은 판단의 기준이 된다
lines: Rather than immediately treating existing skills as worthless, use them to judge what new tools produce.
Apply your knowledge, use the tools and learn how far you can responsibly delegate.

People who understand code can see more in generated code. People who understand art can identify specific problems and possibilities in generated images. People who understand games can consider how a working feature becomes an experience.
As tools advance, the process of making things will change.
Our accumulated skills can find new uses within it.
When using AI, which tasks became easier, and where did you find your own knowledge more necessary?
Share your experience in the comments.
This was Yamyam Coding. Thank you.
